title: The complete early CUE collision process is Poisson

With v=8N^(8/3)a/(72pi)^(2/3), collision times and circular locations converge to a Poisson point process of intensity(3/2)sqrt(v)dv db/(2pi). The number of nonreal conjugate pairs at rescaled time v converges to Poisson(v^(3/2)); the count process has the corresponding finite-dimensional limit, and the kth collision satisfies V_k^(3/2)~Gamma(k,1). The proof exhausts all N roots even after the first complexification.

On a common small tubular analytic neighborhood of each bounded extreme-time interval, its tracked factors have ranks one or two. title: Every Hermite orbital radius is a finite computable Wronskian boundary
statement: For m>=2, let P_m(z)=i^m He_m(z/i), S_m(x)=sum_j exp(i h_mj x)/P_m_prime(i h_mj), and W_mk=det[S_m^(p+q)]_(p,q=0)^k. The Hermite orbital radius r_m is the least positive zero among W_mk for0<=k<=floor((m-2)/2). It equals the extended-Chebyshev critical interval length of ker P_m(D), satisfies pi/h_m<=r_m<=(m-1)pi/h_m, and is uniformly computable in m by certified lower and upper searches. Thus every local constant in NN-A029 is reduced to floor(m/2) explicit one-variable entire functions; no endpoint multiplicity is determined.

Its companion matrix $B_m$ gives the algebraic connection $d-B_m\,dx$ on the trivial rank-$m$ bundle over $\mathbb A^1$. The analytic horizontal sections identify with $\ker P_m(D)$. Evaluation on $\coprod_\ell\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[x]/(x-t_\ell)^{\nu_\ell}$ is the actual Hermite jet map; its determinant is the confluent HCIZ numerator up to explicit nonzero factors. A zero of $W_{m,k}(x)$ means failure for two fat points of lengths $m-1-k$ and $k+1$. The exact orbital boundary is therefore a finite collection of one-variable jet-determinant degeneracies. The connection and finite etale spectral algebra are concrete; no arithmetic Frobenius structure, purity, or polynomial-time algorithm is inferred.

For m=2 modulo4 there are equally many left and right branches; for positive m=0 modulo4 there are m/2+1 left and m/2-1 right branches, since the two vertical first jets bend left. No actual Dirichlet central zero is asserted.

title: All multiple Dirichlet and zeta branches have a nonzero normal jet by second order
statement: At any specified critical-line zero rho=1/2+i gamma of multiplicity m>=2 of a nonprincipal primitive Dirichlet L-function, real or complex, the shifted branches satisfy s_j=rho+c_j*t^(1/m)+(D_rho/m)c_j^2*t^(2/m)+O(t^(3/m)), c_j^m=rho*L(rho+1)/A_m. Unconditionally Re D_rho>m+h_a(gamma)>m, with h_1=pi/(2cosh(pi gamma)) and h_0=1/[2(gamma^2+1/4)]-h_1>0. Thus every vertical first direction bends strictly left and every branch is transverse by second Puiseux order. For Dedekind functions the explicit signature/height bound is proved; for every multiple critical-line zeta zero Re D_rho>m-11/48>0. Under A these statements cover all multiple nontrivial Dirichlet and zeta zeros. The simple-zero second jet has an extra term, so simple-zero transversality is not concluded.
inputs: Unconditional primitive Dirichlet or pole-removed Dedekind completion, vertical reflection, classical critical strip and order-one Hadamard product. A is used only to locate every nontrivial Dirichlet/zeta zero on the line.
Multiplicity m>=2 is essential for the displayed second Puiseux coefficient. Exact gamma recurrence/reflection and NN-A004 shift expansion.
The existing NN-A014 ball gives A0 in(0.0117395,0.0117396) below1/16; positive theta integration then gives gamma^2>8 on the zeta critical line, without a new computation or RH.

geometry_translation: At a critical-line analytic Cartier zero of length $m$, completed reflection puts the first reduced logarithmic coefficient in $i\mathbb R$. In the genus-one factorization, this is exactly the assertion $\Re a=0$ for its exponential factor; reflection pairs $\alpha$ with $-\bar\alpha$, cancelling the real linear constants. The global divisor then gives the strictly positive real logarithmic derivative at displacement one. After $t=u^m$, the local algebra $\mathbb C[z]/(z^m)$ normalizes into $m$ sections. For $m\ge2$, the specified norm shift contributes no $t^2$ term at the second Puiseux order, and the exact gamma correction makes every vertical first direction acquire a strictly negative second normal component in the Dirichlet case and the displayed Dedekind range. SGA~1, Expos\'e~I, section~3, Proposition~1 and section~4, Proposition~10 give the finite differentials and discriminant dictionary. The simple case has an additional shift term; no arithmetic deformation, purity assertion or simple-transversality claim is inferred.

statement: Under A, put c=1/(2*zeta(3))-1/3>1/15. In particular eta=1/30 gives lower bounds4/87 relative to all zero occurrences and2/29 relative to simple zeros. No sign balance, density-one transversality or all-simple assertion is made.

geometry_translation: The analytic zero divisor is counted with its actual local lengths. At a reduced point, $d\zeta_t=\zeta\prime(\rho)\,ds-\rho\zeta(\rho+1)\,dt$, so its section has tangent $\partial_t+v_\rho\partial_s$. The observable $r_\rho=|\Re v_\rho|/|v_\rho|$ is its normalized real normal component relative to the critical line. The theorem proves a positive lower counting-density margin on this reduced locus while retaining every multiplicity in the ambient denominator. SGA~1, Expos\'e~I, section~3, Proposition~1 gives the local differentials dictionary. The characters $x\mapsto e^{i\gamma\log x}$ belong to the compact dual of $\mathbb Q_{>0}$, a product of prime circles. Landau\textquotesingle s fixed-frequency formula and absolute Dirichlet convergence identify the exterior ratio\textquotesingle s Haar constant term as $\sum\mu(n)n^{-3}=1/\zeta(3)$. The deterministic cosine inequality combines this with the single Hardy-phase mean. No Frobenius equidistribution for zeros, arithmetic shifted family, sign-balance law or complexity separation is asserted.

At eta1/4 these are2/15 and1/5. On that counted subset |Re v| is at least a constant times gamma^(1-epsilon), for every fixed epsilon>0. No sign balance or conductor-uniform assertion is made.
